question: Should OpenClaw add a declarative `bindings.match.content` routing contract, or should content-driven routing be owned by a pre-routing plugin hook instead?
rationale: Both paths affect config/API surface, route precedence, message delivery, session state, cache behavior, regex safety, and body rewriting; current code and docs do not settle that product/API choice.

options.title: Resolve API Direction First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose whether declarative binding config or a plugin hook is the canonical routing surface before implementation.

options.title: Approve Binding Matcher
options.body: Add validated `match.content` config with explicit precedence, safe matching rules, cache behavior, docs, generated schema updates, and `stripMatch` semantics.

options.title: Supersede With Plugin Hook
options.body: Close or narrow this issue only after a reviewed pre-routing hook lands and documentation explains how it replaces binding-level content routing.

recommendation.title: Resolve API Direction First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose whether declarative binding config or a plugin hook is the canonical routing surface before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current routing-history and product-review signal for the affected resolver and multi-agent route contract.
